subject: PrivInfra module interface contract review: Terraform/Helm/Ansible handoff

Cc: infra-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Request: review module interface contract for private deploy

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for taking this on. We're finalizing the Acme private deployment for a subset of services and want Redwood's guidance on how your Terraform/Helm/Ansible modules will interoperate with our own provisioning (we're using Crossplane + some legacy Ansible roles).

Primary asks:
- Can you confirm the expected interface (inputs/outputs) for network modules (VPC, VLANs, SR-IOV passthrough) so we can avoid overlapping resources?
- How does Redwood recommend we gate CI for your Helm charts when we have a separate promotion pipeline?
- Any redlines on mutating these modules for on-prem (we need to preserve auditability)?

I've attached our proposed module-interface doc and a network boundary diagram. Would love a short review and a meeting if helpful — this week if possible.

Thanks,
Alice Ng
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Acme Consumer Apps
Attachments: priv-iac-module-interface-spec.docx, network-boundary-diagram.png

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Alice Ng <alice.ng@acme-corp.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: review module interface contract for private deploy

Alice —

Thanks for the doc and the diagram. Happy to review — looping in Irene (priv-deploy lead) and Aditya (network/CI SME).

Proposed cadence: 30-min sync to align on contracts + follow-up with a short checklist we can both sign off on. Our immediate concerns I want to call out before the meeting:
- Interface boundaries: Redwood's Terraform VPC module expects sole ownership of subnet allocation and route-table attachments; we can provide a minimal 'shared-subnet' mode but it requires explicit opt-in and tagging to keep audit traces intact.
- SR-IOV / passthrough: hardware drivers and NIC assignments are considered out-of-band for our Helm chart; we provide annotations for node-level device plugins, but the mapping must be deterministic and recorded in inventory.
- CI gating: we prefer a 'consumer-gated' model — Redwood publishes chart release artifacts (signed), and the customer's promotion pipeline pulls and runs acceptance tests. We can supply a sample gating job that runs the chart dry-run + integration smoke tests.

Irene/Aditya — can you both look at Alice's spec and call out any blocking constraints before we book a slot?

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solution Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachments: none

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, Alice Ng <alice.ng@acme-corp.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:21:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: review module interface contract for private deploy

Thanks — quick tech notes after a first pass on the doc (I focused on Terraform module inputs/outputs and CI hooks):

1) Terraform module contracts
- VPC module: required inputs: cidr_block, region_tag, owner_tag, public_subnet_suffixes (list), private_subnet_suffixes (list). Outputs: vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, route_table_ids, NAT_gateway_ids.
- Shared-subnet mode: must pass explicit "host_reservation" tag and the module will not create subnets; it will only attach route tables and create network-level hooks. This avoids overlapping CIDR claims.

2) Network lifecycle and SR-IOV
- We cannot safely claim SR-IOV device assignments in Terraform across heterogeneous on-prem hardware. Our recommended pattern: provide a mapping file (CSV or inventory) that the Ansible role consumes to label nodes and render device-plugin daemonsets. Helm charts expect node labels like redwood.io/sriov=enabled and redwood.io/sriov-profile={profile}.

3) Helm chart gating & artifact model
- We publish chart tgz + provenance sig (cosign). Customer pipeline should verify signature and run a standard smoke job (provided in ci-gating-example.yaml). We will maintain a compatibility matrix for chart values keys used by private deployments (e.g., enablePersistentKV, nodeAffinity hints).

4) Mutations & auditability
- If you (Acme) need to patch our modules, please fork the repo and submit PRs to our compatibility branch. We will accept customer-maintained forks under a "supported-fork" agreement (we track divergence and give guidance). All changes must be captured in Git with signed commits for audit.

Blocking items I see for the next sprint:
- Confirm CIDR reservation policy (who owns the block).
- Decide whether Acme will run Redwood's acceptance tests in their pipeline or call our hosted test runner (privacy considerations).

I can join a 30-min sync tomorrow morning PDT — suggest 9:30am.

—Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: ci-gating-example.yaml

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Alice Ng <alice.ng@acme-corp.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:11:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: review module interface contract for private deploy

Alice —

Appended a short test matrix and acceptance criteria below (also attached to this thread). Please review and confirm whether these map to your internal SRE/QA responsibilities. If agreed, we'll add the checklist to the PR template so every change to the modules must reference the checklist items.

Acceptance matrix (high level):
- Network contract: Create resource + attach RTs — PASS if subnets and routes created and tagged per spec.
- Shared-subnet mode: PASS if module skips creation and leaves existing resources untouched and tags are present.
- Helm deploy smoke test: Deploy chart with default values + hit a health endpoint. PASS if response 200 within 45s.
- SR-IOV labeling: PASS if nodes are labeled and device-plugin pods reach Running state.

Operational notes:
- We'll require a short migration runbook if you ever change CIDR boundaries.
- For audit logs, we'll include a small wrapper that records who ran the Terraform apply and pushes a summary to your audit collector (we support Splunk/ELK).

If nothing else blocks, I'll create a PR template and a small sample pipeline job this afternoon.

Irene Choi
Sr. PM, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
Attachments: priv-module-acceptance-matrix.csv

Best,
